title: Foundations, Wiener, and first-order cybernetics
summary: Foundational works and translations around Norbert Wiener's first-order cybernetics: control, communication, feedback, prediction, and the social questions raised by automation.
research_use: Use this area to establish the baseline vocabulary of cybernetics and to trace how Wiener's technical framework becomes a broader social theory.

title: French, Soviet, German, and translation contexts
summary: Regional and translation histories showing how cybernetics moved through French, Soviet, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Serbo-Croatian contexts.
research_use: Use this area to compare national receptions, scientific vocabularies, ideological constraints, and translation choices.

title: Macy conferences and the cybernetics group
summary: Works focused on the Macy conferences, the cybernetics group, and the early interdisciplinary network around feedback, communication, psychiatry, anthropology, mathematics, and engineering.
research_use: Use this area to reconstruct people, meetings, disciplinary crossings, and the formation of cybernetics as an interdisciplinary field.

title: Second-order cybernetics, autopoiesis, and constructivism
summary: Observer-centered and self-referential cybernetics: autopoiesis, radical constructivism, self-organization, cognition, embodiment, and epistemology.
research_use: Use this area to track the move from observed systems to observing systems, and from control models to cognition and self-production.

title: Pask, conversation theory, learning, and performance
summary: Gordon Pask's conversation theory, human learning, performance, education, and interaction-oriented cybernetics.
research_use: Use this area for chapters on pedagogy, learning machines, conversation as a formal model, and cybernetics as an interaction discipline.

title: Historiography, Cold War, politics, and critique
summary: Historical analyses of cybernetics as a Cold War science, an epistemic style, a political vocabulary, and an object of later critique.
research_use: Use this area for historiographic framing, political stakes, military and Cold War context, and critiques of cybernetic rationality.

title: Computing, design, media, and counterculture
summary: Cybernetics as a bridge into computing, design research, media theory, counterculture, cultural techniques, and apparatus theories.
research_use: Use this area to connect cybernetics to design methods, computing cultures, media theory, and postwar human-science reform.

title: Posthumanism, cyborgs, and embodied mind
summary: Cybernetics in posthumanist, cyborg, body, embodiment, and cognitive-science lineages.
research_use: Use this area for the cultural afterlife of cybernetics in body theory, cyborg studies, posthumanism, and embodied cognition.

title: Social impact, governance, and state-of-the-art surveys
summary: Works that generalize cybernetics into social organization, governance, control societies, communications revolution, and survey/state-of-the-field contexts.
research_use: Use this area for macro-social arguments and for synthesizing cybernetics as a historical force in organizations, markets, states, and institutions.

title: Periodicals, diagrams, bibliographies, and research resources
summary: Journals, diagrams, resource documents, bibliographies, and short-form materials that help map the field rather than presenting a single monograph argument.
research_use: Use this area for field mapping, citation discovery, visualizations, and quick orientation documents.
